label: b1-check-R3
text:
These rules are for the agent's later session in /workspace. They do not apply to you: implement system enforcement for each rule with its enforcer, at its trigger, on its target.

Rule R3: 在生成的代码文件里，缩进必须严格保持为 4 个空格

- Route: Regex validator (Validation › Regex › Regex validator) · File write / edit (Agent action › File write / edit), timing: after · Source file (Source code › Source file)
- The check, by the enforcer: A regular expression that the checked text must match, or must not match. A match against the rule is a violation. What is read is part of the enforcer: a whole file, each line, only comments, a reply, the start or the end of a text. Check: a check script (/opt/enforce-toolbox/skeletons/check.py) with a regular expression; read what the rule is about (the whole text, each line, comments, the start or the end). Start from the skeleton: /opt/enforce-toolbox/skeletons/regex_validator.py
- Where it runs, by the trigger: the framework's hook (/opt/enforce-toolbox/mechanisms/framework-hooks.md) at the end of the turn (every file); git hooks (/opt/enforce-toolbox/mechanisms/git-hooks.md) (at commit); checks that keep running (/opt/enforce-toolbox/mechanisms/keep-running.md)
- What it reads, by the target: A source code file. Where: /workspace/<path>, on disk for every mechanism; the content of a write before it happens: only the framework's hook (/opt/enforce-toolbox/mechanisms/framework-hooks.md) before its write tool Which files: decide when the check runs, from the file in hand: the files the agent will create cannot be known before. Map its name, or its content, to a language with a complete list, such as Pygments (`get_lexer_for_filename`, `guess_lexer`) or GitHub Linguist's list of languages: programming and markup languages that hold code count (Python, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, shell, …); documents and data do not (Markdown, plain text, JSON, YAML, CSV), unless the rule names them. A rule about the file itself (its first lines, its name, its encoding) applies once per file, in that file's own comment syntax (in HTML, an HTML comment); a rule about the code in it (functions, names, statements) also reaches code embedded in another file, such as a `<script>` in HTML. A file whose kind is unknown is checked, not passed.
- Tools: none to install
- Toolbox nodes: /opt/enforce-toolbox/enforcers/validation/regex/regex-validator.md, /opt/enforce-toolbox/triggers/agent-action/file-write-edit.md, /opt/enforce-toolbox/targets/source-code/source-file.md

The work for these rules comes as nodes, one at a time; when you reply to a node, the harness checks it. The nodes: check-R3, binding-1.
Build exactly what each rule's route says. If a part of a route cannot work here, write why in /opt/enforce/deviations.json ({"R<n>": "<why>"}) and build the nearest thing that keeps the rest of the route.


Node check-R3 (1 of 2): write test cases and the check of R3. The cases: at least two that break the rule, as files in /opt/enforce/fixtures/R3/flag, and at least two that follow it, in /opt/enforce/fixtures/R3/pass; each one file of what the check reads (A source code file. A file whose kind is unknown is checked, not passed.). Cover every kind of input the rule reaches, as the agent may really write it: for files, several languages each in its own comment syntax (Python, JavaScript, HTML with a <script>, a shell script, …), and also files the rule does not cover, which must pass; for a reply, short and long replies, with lists and code blocks. The check: the executable /opt/enforce/checks/R3; `/opt/enforce/checks/R3 <file>` exits 0 when the file follows the rule, and otherwise exits 1 and prints each violation: R3, where (the file and line, or the part of the text), and what to change. Done when: /opt/enforce/fixtures/R3/flag and /opt/enforce/fixtures/R3/pass each hold at least two files; as the agent, the check exits 1 and names R3 for every file in /opt/enforce/fixtures/R3/flag, and exits 0 for every file in /opt/enforce/fixtures/R3/pass. The harness checks this when you reply.
